title: DNA Extraction from Sterivex Filters
author: Christopher Neil Thornton
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bm2ek8be
materials: Gently shake a few times and centrifuge.
Invert a few times to mix.

steps.title: Add DEB and store
steps.instruction: Add 1.4 mL of DEB to each Sterivex filter using a syringe and needle; position the needle just below the filter mouth and stop when the solution covers the white filter (do not fill to the top). Store the filter at –20 °C if stopping here.

steps.title: Place filter in perforated tube
steps.instruction: Insert each Sterivex filter into a 50 mL tube that has holes (to allow liquid flow).

steps.title: Heat incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate the tube at 65 °C for 30 minutes on a Genemate spinning machine.

steps.title: Vortex filter (bead beating)
steps.instruction: Vortex each Sterivex (still inside the Falcon tube) for 30 seconds.

steps.title: Transfer lysate to bead tube
steps.instruction: Using a syringe, withdraw the fluid from each Sterivex and eject it into a bead‑beating tube containing 0.1 mm glass beads for bacteria.

steps.title: Centrifuge and collect supernatant
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the bead tube for 2 minutes at 5,000 g. Transfer the fluid (avoiding the beads) into a fresh Eppendorf tube, adding no more than 900 µL per tube (or no more than 750 µL if using 1.5 mL tubes).

steps.title: Phenol‑chloroform extraction
steps.instruction: Perform a two‑phase extraction to remove proteins and lipids.

substeps.instruction: Add an equal volume of phenol/chloroform/isoamyl alcohol (25:24:1, pre‑mixed with alkaline buffer) to each tube.
Gently shake a few times and centrifuge at 14,000 g for 1 minute.
Transfer the aqueous supernatant to a fresh tube.
Add an equal volume of chloroform/isoamyl alcohol (24:1) to the transferred aqueous phase.
Centrifuge briefly (as above) and carefully remove the supernatant to a new tube, avoiding the bottom organic layer.

steps.title: Redistribute aqueous phase
steps.instruction: Divide the aqueous phase among up to three tubes so that each 2.0 mL tube receives ≤550 µL (or each 1.6 mL tube ≤450 µL). If no additional salt is needed, you may skip sodium acetate and add up to 600 µL in a 2.0 mL tube.

steps.title: Add salt and ethanol
steps.instruction: To each tube add 0.1 × volume of 3 M sodium acetate (pH 5.2) (e.g., 55 µL to 550 µL) and then 2 × volume of 100 % ethanol (e.g., 1 210 µL to 605 µL). For low‑biomass samples optionally add 1.2 µL glycogen (20 µg/µL).

steps.title: Precipitate DNA at –20 °C
steps.instruction: Incubate the mixture at –20 °C for at least 1 hour or overnight (ice incubation is an alternative). Then centrifuge for 40 minutes at 16 000 g (optionally using a cooled centrifuge at 0 °C).

steps.title: Wash pellet with 70 % ethanol
steps.instruction: Carefully pour off the supernatant without inverting the tube; keep it at a gentle angle. Add 500 µL cold 70 % ethanol, invert to mix and ensure the pellet is fully dislodged.

steps.title: Second ethanol wash and spin
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 16 000 g for 10 minutes, then remove the liquid with a pipettor being careful not to disturb the pellet.

steps.title: Dry pellet in Vacufuge
steps.instruction: Place tubes with open lids in a Vacufuge and spin for 7 minutes at 30 °C on the V‑AL setting. If ethanol is still visible, spin an additional 2–5 minutes. Stop if pellets become powdery (over‑dry).

steps.title: Resuspend DNA in low EDTA TE
steps.instruction: Resuspend the dried pellet in ~100 µL low‑EDTA TE buffer and heat at 55 °C until fully dissolved (≈10 minutes).

steps.title: Prepare low EDTA TE buffer
steps.instruction: Make 10 mM Tris‑HCl, 0.1 mM EDTA (pH 8.0): for 50 mL, combine 500 µL 1 M Tris‑HCl (autoclaved) with 10 µL 0.5 M EDTA (autoclaved), add Milli‑Q water to 50 mL, and filter‑sterilize through a 0.22 µm syringe filter.

steps.title: Store DNA
steps.instruction: Store the resuspended DNA at 4 °C for short‑term use or at –20 °C/–80 °C for long‑term storage; avoid repeated freeze‑thaw cycles. Optionally keep half at 4 °C (working sample) and half at –80 °C (archive).
